Hey Dylan —

Thanks for the earlier demo. We’re keen to move from PoC -> production, but procurement needs a clear mutual action plan (MAP) that ties milestones to committed capacity and pricing. High level asks:
- Evaluation plan (2–6 week ramp) with pass/fail gates
- GPU pool sizing guidance for our expected workload (batch inference for perception + some online low-latency calls)
- Pricing for reserved capacity (1yr vs 2yr), and burst clauses for temporary overage
- Target close window: ideally by end of August so we can hit Q3 launch

Can you send a proposed MAP + pricing playbook? I’ll loop in Mike (CFO) if numbers look reasonable.

Thanks,

Liz — thanks, this is exactly the kind of structure we prefer. I’ve attached a draft MAP and a high-level pricing tiers workbook to get us started. Key notes up front:
- Proposed evaluation: 4-week staged plan (week 0 onboarding + perf baseline, week 1–2 scale tests, week 3 cost/perf tuning, week 4 sign-off)
- Sizing: recommend starting with a 4x A100-equivalent pool (estimated steady-state: 120 p99 concurrent tokens/sec) with burst capacity up to +50% for 72 hours across a 90-day window
- Pricing: 12-month and 24-month reserved rates included; deeper discount at 24mo commit and at higher GPU-count bands; explicit burst billing metric (per-minute incremental) to avoid sticker shock

Next steps I propose:
1) Quick sync with Neha (SE) to validate sizing assumptions — Tue or Wed?
2) We’ll update the MAP with milestone-level acceptance criteria and delivery owners
3) Marissa to share playbook language for commercial terms we need in procurement review

Attachments: redwood_map_draft.pdf, pricing-tiers-commitments.xlsx

Best,
Dylan

Folks — following up with a short sizing estimate. I ran your traffic profile from the PoC and made two configs: conservative (start small, scale quickly) and aggressive (capacity for launch traffic).

Conservative: 2x A100-equivalent nodes; target 95th percentile latency 120ms; supports baseline batch/online split 70/30.
Aggressive (recommended for Q3 launch): 4x A100-equivalent nodes; supports headroom for sudden teleops bursts; recommended to negotiate 24-week ramping credit for first 8 weeks.

Burst clause options:
- Option A: Pre-approved burst pool equal to +50% capacity for up to 72 continuous hours per quarter at 1.8x per-minute rate
- Option B: Auto-scale into on-demand at market rates (no commit) with soft limit alerts at 80% pool utilization

I attached the spreadsheet with the per-model token/s cost lines and calibration scripts we’ll run during the eval. Happy to walk through on the sync — Wed 10am PT works for me.

Neha
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Team — pricing guardrails to include in the MAP for procurement:

Commit tiers (examples, shown per-GPU monthly):
- Tier 1 (2–3 GPUs, 12mo): $2,900 / GPU / mo (baseline)
- Tier 2 (4–9 GPUs, 12mo): $2,350 / GPU / mo (-19% vs Tier 1)
- Tier 3 (10+ GPUs, 12mo): $1,950 / GPU / mo (-33% vs Tier 1)

24-month commitments: additional 10% off list at each tier (applies to committed portion).

Ramp & credits: for customers who need staged ramp we can provide a ramp-credit that converts to monthly credit over first 8 weeks (reduces initial burn while they ramp load onto the dedicated pool).

Burst clause (recommended wording):
- Customer allowed up to 50% temporary burst above committed pool for up to 72 hours per rolling 90-day window at 1.8x committed unit rate; any sustained usage beyond that window auto-billed at on-demand published rate and triggers capacity review.

Contractual ask: procurement usually wants firming language around minimum monthly commitment and clear overage rates. I’ve dropped a template clause in the shared Drive.

Sean Gallagher
Director, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
